sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- coalition] Footage released Sunday evening shows what the coalition describes as the destruction of vital Ansar Allah resources in Hodeidah and Dhamar provinces, the same Sunday-morning operation recorded at 1900-02. [ATTRIBUTED COUNTER-CLAIM -- Al-Masirah via Shafaq, NOT independently confirmed] Two Saudi airstrikes struck an oil company station in Bajil district, Hodeidah, wounding three civilians; two more hit the Faculty of Medicine at Hodeidah University, with no casualties reported. [ATTRIBUTED THREAT -- Ansar Allah military source via Saba] A Ansar Allah source threatened to target Saudi Aramco facilities, warned investors of potential losses, and urged international airlines to avoid Saudi airspace except over Mecca and Medina. [CONTEXT -- pre-window Saturday claim, Saree] Ansar Allah spokesman Yahya Saree on Saturday accused Saudi Arabia of 66 strikes in the prior 24 hours and put total Saudi strikes since the latest escalation at 3,755. PortWatch backbone: newest snapshot remains portwatch-2026-10-26.json, observations Oct 18, stale=true -- Bab el-Mandeb counted figure cited only as stale (see hidden_constraint).
sections.what_verified: Coalition statement carried by Gulf News (T3) in addition to the coalition primary itself; Al-Masirah counter-claims are a conflicting account of the same operation, not corroboration of the coalition's target set
sections.what_disputed: Al-Masirah's account directly contests the 'precision / vital resources' framing by naming an oil-company station and a university medical faculty as hit, with 3 civilians wounded in Bajil. Neither side's site list is independently verified in-window.
sections.why_matters: Riyadh shows the footage; Sanaa names the targets -- an oil station and a medical faculty. Same Sunday operation, two opposite stories, and the Red Sea lane in the middle.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW UPDATE to 1900-02 (Gulf News footage release 19:41 ; Shafaq 19:20 ) -- Coalition releases footage of Sunday precision strikes in Hodeidah and Dhamar; Ansar Allah-affiliated Al-Masirah counters that an oil-company station in Bajil and Hodeidah University's Faculty of Medicine were hit, 3 civilians wounded

totw_analysis: Our read: Riyadh shows the footage; Sanaa names the targets -- an oil station and a medical faculty. Same Sunday operation, two opposite stories, and the Red Sea lane in the middle. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Precision strike on war resources -- or civilian infrastructure hit? The footage proves strikes happened; it does not settle what was hit.
